scope.current_boundary: Teach qualitative understanding of frictional forces between solid surfaces (static vs kinetic, opposes relative motion, energy converted to thermal energy) and viscous/drag forces in fluids (liquids and gases, air resistance, simple model of drag increasing as speed increases, dependence on shape/area and fluid density, absence of coefficients of friction or viscosity). Do not pre-teach vertical motion graphs under air resistance, terminal velocity derivation, parachute deployment dynamics, or conservation of momentum.
prior_scope_summaries_consulted: Assumes mastery of lesson 9702_t03_cm01_l01: mass as inertia, F = ma for constant mass.
Assumes mastery of lesson 9702_t03_cm01_l02: linear momentum p = mv, force as rate of change of momentum.
Assumes mastery of lesson 9702_t03_cm01_l03: Newton's three laws of motion, weight W = mg, action-reaction pairs.

immediate_previous.boundary: Each of Newton's laws of motion: formal statement and application; weight as gravitational force W = mg.
can_assume: Newton's first, second, and third laws of motion
weight as effect of gravitational field on mass, W = mg
resultant force as vector sum of all forces
acceleration always in the same direction as resultant force
linear momentum p = mv and force as rate of change of momentum

immediate_next.boundary: Qualitatively the motion of objects in a uniform gravitational field with air resistance; reaching terminal velocity.
must_not_preteach: complete stage-by-stage motion of falling objects reaching terminal velocity
motion graphs (s-t, v-t, a-t) of falling bodies in air vs vacuum
parachute opening dynamics and second terminal velocity plateau
principle of conservation of momentum (Topic 3 module 3)

selection_dimensions: Components: P1 (multiple choice) and P2 (structured theory)
Years: 2016 to 2024 across February/March and May/June series
Archetypes: explanation, direct calculation, comparison, graph interpretation, force vector analysis
Representations: diver in water, trolley on slope with friction and air resistance, descending submarine, car braking, falling sphere

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Directly tests that as speed of an object in a fluid decreases, viscous drag force decreases.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Describe and explain the variation of viscous drag force acting on a diver in water as speed decreases.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Speed decreases, so viscous force / drag force decreases.
lesson_sections_informed: Viscous and drag forces in fluids
Worked Example 2: Diver plunging through water

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Tests distinguishing constant solid friction from speed-dependent air resistance on a moving trolley.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Explain why assuming constant total resistive force is incorrect when speed increases.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Air resistance increases as speed increases, so total resistive force increases.
lesson_sections_informed: Comparing solid friction and fluid drag
Worked Example 3: Cyclist on a level road

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Applies viscous drag opposing motion in water alongside weight and upthrust at constant velocity.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Relate magnitudes of weight, upthrust, and viscous drag for a submarine descending at constant velocity.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Weight = Upthrust + Viscous drag, so weight > upthrust.
lesson_sections_informed: Check 4: Submarine moving at steady depth

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Emphasizes that drag force requires an atmosphere/fluid medium; without air, horizontal resistive force is zero.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Identify horizontal and vertical forces on a projectile in a vacuum.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: No air means zero drag horizontally; only gravity acts vertically.
lesson_sections_informed: Viscous and drag forces in fluids
Mistake 3: Believing drag forces exist when an object is at rest

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Illustrates relationship between increasing braking resistive force and decreasing speed.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Relate increasing braking force to non-uniform deceleration and velocity-time graph curvature.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Increasing braking force means increasing deceleration, giving increasing negative slope on v-t graph.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Force vector analysis showing upward air resistance opposing downward weight during acceleration.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Identify forces acting on a sphere falling in air before terminal velocity is reached.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Downward weight exceeds upward air resistance during downward acceleration.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Deals with drag balancing gravity at terminal velocity; context informs drag opposing motion, full analysis handed off to Lesson 5.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Magnitude of air resistance and acceleration at terminal velocity.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: At terminal velocity, air resistance equals mg and acceleration is zero.

question_parts_inspected.decision_reason: Specific to parachute opening dynamics and subsequent terminal velocity, which belongs strictly to Lesson 5.
question_parts_inspected.assessed_demand: Determine direction and magnitude change of velocity immediately after parachute opening.
question_parts_inspected.reasoning_or_distractor: Velocity remains downward while decreasing in magnitude.
